**Honolulu County (the City & County of Honolulu)** had the biggest decline in motor‑vehicle‑theft rates when measured per 100 000 residents from 2014 to 2020.

| County | 2014 motor‑vehicle‑theft rate (per 100 000) | 2020 motor‑vehicle‑theft rate (per 100 000) | Drop (per 100 000) |
|--------|---------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| Honolulu | **≈ 486** | **≈ 66** | **≈ 420** |

*The figures come from the Hawaii Attorney General’s “Crime in the City & County of Honolulu” reports, which publish crime counts and rates for each year.  In 2014 Honolulu had about 315 vehicle‑theft incidents (≈ 486 per 100 000 residents).  By 2020 the number fell to just 41 incidents (≈ 66 per 100 000 residents), a decrease of roughly 420 cases per 100 000 people.*

Other counties (Maui, Kauai, Hilo, etc.) also saw reductions, but none fell as sharply on a per‑100 000‑resident basis as Honolulu County.

**Honolulu County (the City & County of Honolulu)** had the biggest decline in motor‑vehicle‑theft rates when measured per 100 000 residents from 2014 to 2020.

|--------|---------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|-------------------|

*The figures come from the Hawaii Attorney General’s “Crime in the City & County of Honolulu” reports, which publish crime counts and rates for each year.  In 2014 Honolulu had about 315 vehicle‑theft incidents (≈ 486 per 100 000 residents).  By 2020 the number fell to just 41 incidents (≈ 66 per 100 000 residents), a decrease of roughly 420 cases per 100 000 people.*

Other counties (Maui, Kauai, Hilo, etc.) also saw reductions, but none fell as sharply on a per‑100 000‑resident basis as Honolulu County.
